intro_to_like.label: LIKE and Wildcards
intro_to_like.summary: Use LIKE with % for variable-length text and _ for exactly one character.

sc_like_prefix.title: Pattern for a starting text match
sc_like_prefix.prompt: Which pattern matches city values that start with `Chi`?
sc_like_prefix.hint: Use the wildcard that allows any number of characters after `Chi`.

help.concept: `LIKE` uses `%` to match any number of characters. To match text that begins with a fixed starting part, put `%` after that starting text.
help.hint_1: You want values that begin with `Chi`, so the pattern should keep `Chi` at the front.
help.hint_2: The correct pattern has `Chi` first and then a wildcard for the rest of the text.

fb_like_contains.title: Complete a contains pattern
fb_like_contains.prompt: Fill in the missing pattern so the query matches names containing the letter `a` anywhere.
fb_like_contains.hint: A contains pattern usually needs wildcards on both sides of the text.

help.concept: To match text anywhere inside a value, place `%` before and after the target text.
help.hint_1: The letter `a` should stay in the middle of the pattern.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that allows characters both before and after `a`.

sc_1.title: Meaning of one underscore
sc_1.prompt: In a SQL `LIKE` pattern, what does `_` represent?
sc_1.hint: Think about how many characters `_` stands for in a text pattern.

help.concept: The underscore wildcard in `LIKE` matches one and only one character, unlike `%`, which can match many characters.
help.hint_1: Compare `_` with `%`: one is fixed-length for a single character, and the other is variable-length.
help.hint_2: If a pattern has three underscores, it requires exactly three characters in that position.

fb_2.title: Choose the exact-length pattern
fb_2.prompt: Fill in the blank to match emails with exactly 4 characters before `@example.com`.
fb_2.hint: Count how many single-character slots are needed before `@example.com`.

help.concept: Multiple underscores in a `LIKE` pattern enforce an exact number of characters in that position.
help.hint_1: You need one underscore for each character before the `@` sign.
help.hint_2: The matching choice has four underscores and no percent sign.

try-intro_to_like-sketch0.title: Find Customer Names Beginning with M
try-intro_to_like-sketch0.prompt: Prepare an alphabetical outreach slice. Return `id`, `full_name`, and `city` from `customers`, in that order. Use `LIKE` so only names beginning with `M` remain.
try-intro_to_like-sketch0.hint: For a prefix match, place the fixed starting text before `%`.

help.concept: A trailing percent wildcard lets a LIKE pattern keep any text that begins with the required prefix.
help.hint_1: For a prefix match, place the fixed starting text before `%`.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned columns and rows with the expected result.

try-intro_to_like-sketch0.starterCode:
-- Find customers whose full name begins with M.
SELECT id, full_name, city
FROM customers
WHERE full_name LIKE '';

sourceChecks.message: Use the `customers` table in the FROM clause.
Select the required columns in the requested order: `id`, `full_name`, `city`.
Use `LIKE` for the requested text pattern.

practice-like-single-character.title: Practice: Match one character with _
practice-like-single-character.prompt: Return `full_name` and `city` from `customers`, in that order. Match city values shaped like `H`, exactly one unknown character, then `uston`.
practice-like-single-character.hint: Use the wildcard that represents exactly one character.

help.concept: Each underscore in a LIKE pattern requires exactly one character.
help.hint_1: The unknown position is between `H` and `uston`.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned columns and rows with the expected result.

practice-like-single-character.starterCode:
-- Match one unknown character inside Houston.
SELECT full_name, city
FROM customers
WHERE city LIKE '';

sourceChecks.message: Use the `customers` table in the FROM clause.
Select the required columns in the requested order: `full_name`, `city`.
Use LIKE with `_` for the requested one-character wildcard.

like_text_pattern.title: Match text with LIKE and %
like_text_pattern.bodyMarkdown:
`LIKE` matches a text pattern instead of one exact value.

Use `%` when any number of characters may appear:

- `'A%'` — starts with A
- `'%son'` — ends with son
- `'%art%'` — contains art

Use equality when the whole value must match exactly; use LIKE when the text shape matters.

percent_wildcard_patterns.title: Use _ for one character
percent_wildcard_patterns.bodyMarkdown:
The `_` wildcard matches **exactly one character**.

For example, a pattern such as `'A_'` matches two-character values that begin with A.

Use `%` for variable-length text and `_` for one unknown position. They can appear in the same LIKE pattern when both behaviors are needed.
